A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 2BY2 dataset and two-step object-assembly method. Their complete main text, Appendix A, figures, tables and equations support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, real-world robot trials and ablations, including appendix Chamfer-distance results in Tables 6 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, robot trials and ablations reported in Tables 3-7.

M1.justification: Sections 5 and A.2 retain the same two-step architecture, two-scale VN DGCNN encoder, cross-object fusion, pose heads, losses and training/inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 517 object pairs, 18 fine-grained tasks, grouped-category and All evaluations, and Cup, Flower, Bread and Plug robot tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 6 retain Jigsaw, Puzzlefusion++, Neural Shape Mating and SE(3)-Assembly. The robot comparator and encoder-ablation comparators also remain unchanged. Newly added citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The data splits, SO(3) augmentation, RMSE and Chamfer-distance metrics, batch size 4, learning rate 1e-4, 1,000 training epochs and ten initial robot poses per task remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The encoder and two-step ablations in Tables 5 and 7, geometric-diversity analyses, and qualitative comparisons in Figures 6 and 9 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Robot trial counts and success-rate reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries in Tables 3-7 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains overall robot success rates of 77.5% for the proposed method and 22.5% for SE(3)-Assembly.

T1.justification: The problem and canonical-pose definitions and Equations 1-7 remain unchanged, including the equivariance statements, pose losses and Chamfer-distance formulation. No proofs or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset-novelty, two-step-method, state-of-the-art performance and real-world generalization claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of sequential prediction and equivariance, interpretations of generalization, and Appendix A.5 limitations concerning dataset scope, prescribed grasps and computational efficiency remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's project-page link for further details and demonstrations without supplying a replacement. Implementation, data-processing, training and hardware disclosures are otherwise unchanged. This deletion does not establish that the external resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds citations to Pix2Act, BEAR, generalizable hierarchical skill learning, EquAct and tactile rotation correction (v2 references 24, 43, 73, 76 and 78). These extend the cited literature without changing the surrounding positioning argument.

P1.justification: The abstract loses its closing project-link sentence. Apart from citation edits, the main-text and appendix wording and section organization are retained; there is no substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: The nine figures and seven tables retain their content and page assignments. v2 removes printed page numbers and makes small spacing and text-flow changes, including in the references.

improvement.justification: The method, experimental evidence, results and limitations are unchanged. Five added citations modestly update literature coverage, while removal of the project/demo link slightly reduces resource discoverability. These peripheral edits and minor reformatting do not meaningfully change the paper's overall scientific quality or clarity.
